title: Satellites, 6G Patents and AI Calls: Akash Ambani Lays Out Jio's Next Bets
excerpt: At the India Mobile Congress, the Jio chairman described an indigenous satellite stack, pre-6G patent filings tied to India's 10% global target, and AI built into voice and data services.
body:
• Reliance Jio is building an indigenous satellite communications stack in India and has already filed patents in pre-6G technology, chairman Akash Ambani said at the India Mobile Congress in New Delhi.
  • Jio's display outlined a proposed constellation of about 1,600 low-earth-orbit satellites and 23 ground stations aimed at connecting more than 600,000 villages, including maritime and border areas.
  • Ambani tied Jio's patent push to the government's target of India producing 10% of global 6G patents, and said AI will be built into Jio's voice and data services.
  • No launch timeline was given for satellite services, which Ambani described as an extension of Jio's home broadband push and subject to regulatory approvals.

Satellites, a network that does not exist yet, and artificial intelligence inside ordinary phone calls. Those are the three bets Akash Ambani laid out for Reliance Jio at the 10th India Mobile Congress in New Delhi, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 8 under the theme "Scale Without Boundaries."

"What we're also showing is the progress that we're making on satellite technologies and what we can prove to be an indigenous satellite stack based out of India," Ambani told ANI on the sidelines of the event, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Bet One: Satellites, Built in India

Jio's satellite programme is positioned as broadband infrastructure, not a novelty. Ambani described satellite services as an extension of Jio's broadband push with home broadband as a main use, and said the company had demonstrated its progress to the communications minister while regulatory approvals move ahead, according to reporting summarised by Daily Prabhat. He gave no launch date.

The scale on display was specific. Jio showed a proposed constellation of about 1,600 low-earth-orbit satellites and 23 ground stations across India, aimed at connecting more than 600,000 villages, including maritime and border areas. Those figures are Jio's proposed plan as shown at the event, not a deployed network, and they set up a direct contest with global satellite broadband operators seeking Indian licences.

Bet Two: Patents for 6G, Filed Early

"In fact, in our pre-6G time, we've already filed for patents."

— Akash Ambani, Chairman, Reliance Jio Infocomm

"Like the Prime Minister has said that we want to lead the world when it comes to 6G, and he set a target of 10 per cent of the 6G patents to be coming out of India; we're going to contribute to that story heavily," Ambani said. The filings sit inside a much larger portfolio: Jio Platforms had filed 6,817 patents by March 31, 2026, of which 1,009 had been granted, according to company figures.

The strategy is standards, not just spectrum. Patents filed before 6G is standardised can become essential to the standard itself, which is how a late entrant to global telecom ends up collecting, rather than paying, intellectual property rents in the next cycle.

Bet Three: AI in the Call Itself

The third bet is the closest to the customer. "We really believe that we can innovate on the voice service on the data service using AI. We believe that would be very beneficial to all of the Indian consumers," Ambani said. Jio has not detailed which AI features reach subscribers first, but the direction, intelligence inside basic voice and data rather than only in apps layered on top, is the consumer-facing half of the pitch.

What's Next

Satellite broadband in India still runs through licensing and spectrum decisions in New Delhi, and 6G standards are years from completion. What Ambani's outline does is put Jio's claims on record early: an Indian-built satellite stack, a patent position staked before the standard exists, and AI as a network feature. Each will be judged on delivery, not display boards.
